## Your Chrome, per task

Issue #3: an agent may use the person's own Chrome **per task, when the person allows it** —
never by default, never for good. Under jelly (the plugin sees jelly's engine hand-off) and in real mode, the plugin
wraps the executor of every tool the browse server exposes — each `browse_*` id and anything in the `browse`
namespace, classified or not — the one place Code Mode (the model's only way to reach browse) and the `browse.tools`
RPC both pass through. A call from a conversation with no grant never reaches the MCP server.

- **A task** is one OpenCode session (the conversation) and the agent that runs it.
- **The ask.** The first gated call records `{ id, agent, task, origins, mode, at, expiresAt }` — the task is the
  session's title, the origins are the `allowedOrigins` of a `session_new` or `session_allowlist`, else any site —
  and waits for the person until `expiresAt`, five minutes on. A cancelled turn withdraws it. It is also filed once as the `chrome-ask` notice
  (`jelly.core` request, kind `notice`, category `request`), which jelly raises to the agent's people whatever the
  agent's access level, and keeps for the Inbox. It is filed with `keep`, so a host that is away when it is filed
  still raises it once it reads the pending requests.
- **The mode, enforced.** The call that asks states the mode: a tool of the `read` class in the plugin's own table
  (`status`, `session_list`, `secrets_list`, `secrets_status`) asks to `read`; any other tool, and any tool the table
  does not classify, asks to `act`. Under a `read` grant only those four pass; an act call there never reaches the
  server: it asks again, for `act`, riding along on the task, and waits. Allowed, the same task acts; Not now leaves
  it reading. browse has no separate navigate, snapshot or screenshot tool — they are `execute`, which can click and
  type — so a read grant cannot open or read a page, and the person reads its mode as "to check your Chrome's status
  only; it can't open or read pages" until browse has read-only page tools. A read-only browse session (`session_new` with `readOnly`) refuses
  input, not page script, so it is not counted as read.
- **More than one task.** While a task holds the Chrome, Stop always stays reachable: the read keeps that task's
  state and adds a second conversation's or a subagent's waiting ask as `request`. That ask reaches the person through
  the notice, the Inbox and the plugin's page, which allows it by its id; unanswered, it ends at `expiresAt` as
  Not now.
- **Allow for this task** is `browser.allow { id }` (B3), or jelly's Connect (`browser.connect`), which allows the ask
  named by `input.ask`, or the oldest one when jelly sends `{}`, until jelly draws `asking`. **Not now** is
  `browser.decline { id }`. With no ask pending the read reports `canControl: false`, so jelly offers no Connect and
  the Chrome cannot be allowed in advance.
- **The end.** The agent's `session_reset` or `session_delete` in that conversation, `browser.stop` (all, or one
  `session`), the conversation deleted or archived, an hour with no browse call, or the engine stopping. A call
  still running is aborted with the grant and fails with `CHROME_NOT_ALLOWED`. Nothing is
  written: no rule, saved approval or file, so an "Always allow" on a tool's card never allows the Chrome.
- **The sites.** Under a grant with sites, a `session_new` without an allowlist gets them, and a wider or cleared
  allowlist is refused with `CHROME_SCOPE`.

Managed mode is not the person's Chrome and is not gated. Outside jelly nothing is gated.

## The personal-browser binding

jelly's asks B1–B4 (issue #5), checked against jelly at `99cd657c4`. `nativeData` is jelly's D103 example, exactly
(B1); its `actions` object is strict in jelly's schema, so it names connect and stop only:

```json
[{ "v": 1, "capability": "personal-browser", "view": "browser-native", "read": "browser.status",
   "actions": { "connect": "browser.connect", "stop": "browser.stop" } }]
```

The plugin registers its RPC under the package name, `@joe-broadhead/opencode-browse`:

| Method | Kind | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `browser.status` | read-only, permission `browse_status` | `{ state, canControl, task?, agent?, request? }` (B2, B3) |
| `browser.ask` | read-only, the confirmations' `preview` | the ask in words: agent, mode, task, sites |
| `browser.inbox` | read-only, `inbox.method` | `{ items }`: one `request` item, kind `chrome-ask`, per waiting ask |
| `act.browser.connect` | action, `local`, `always` | `true` when it allowed an ask |
| `act.browser.allow` | action, `local`, `always`, input `{ id }` | `true`; `REQUEST_EXPIRED` or `NOT_YOUR_REQUEST` |
| `act.browser.decline` | action, `local`, `always`, input `{ id }` | `true`; `REQUEST_EXPIRED` or `NOT_YOUR_REQUEST` |
| `act.browser.stop` | action, `local`, `always` | `true` |

The read (B2): `task` is `{ id, title, startedAt }` while `driving` (the plugin never reports `needs-you`), with
`id` the grant's own id and `title` the conversation's; `agent` is the id of the agent holding the session, while a
task is allowed. `request` (B3) is `{ id, agent, task: { title }, scope: { sites, mode }, expiresAt }`, where
`sites: ["*"]` means any site. No other field is reported.

The states: `unavailable` in managed mode or with no binary; `ready` or `driving` (a call in flight) with
`canControl: true` while a task is allowed, with a new `request` riding along, so jelly keeps offering Stop; with no
task and a request waiting, `asking` — reported as `not-connected` (or `extension-needed`) until jelly draws
`asking`, because jelly at `99cd657c4` reads an unknown state as unavailable with neither Connect nor Stop (one
constant, `ASKING_STATE`, in `src/jelly/native.ts`); with neither, `ready` with `canControl: false`, so the next
read after a task ends is `ready`, never `driving` on a stale allow — or `extension-needed` with `canControl: false`
when the running relay reports the extension not connected (a relay that is not running starts on demand, so it
does not make the read `extension-needed`). `REQUEST_EXPIRED` answers an id in the plugin's form
(`ask_` and 24 hex) that is not waiting: answered, withdrawn, run out, or no longer known after an engine restart —
the engine cannot tell them apart, and the next step is the same. `NOT_YOUR_REQUEST` answers only an id the plugin
could never have issued. The page offers Allow for this task, Not now and Stop whenever each
applies. Each action checks jelly's grant before it changes anything: the host's
Ed25519 key published in the engine, the audience `@joe-broadhead/opencode-browse#engine`, the action, the input's
digest, the minute it is good for, the single-use id, and the `local` class the actions declare (jelly's host is what
refuses a `local` action from a paired device).

`browser-native` is a `settings-section` page (`views/browser.html`) with the `rpc` grant for `browser.status` and
`browser.ask`: it shows the state and the request, and offers Allow for this task, Not now and Stop through the
actions, which jelly confirms.

`notices` declares one: `chrome-ask` (label "Your Chrome", category `request`, preview `line`), the ask itself,
naming the agent, the task, the sites and the mode, so the person sees it whatever the agent's access level.

B4's `personal-browser` change signal is built but neither raised nor declared. It would be filed with no name and no
line, keyed per change, not kept, each time the read's answer changes, so jelly reads again at once; it stays separate
from `chrome-ask` because the ask must carry words to the person and the signal must carry none. jelly's notice schema
at `99cd657c4` has no `browser` category and requires a label and a preview: declared as a `request`, each change
would be a banner (one per browse call, as `driving` comes and goes). When jelly treats it as a signal to read, set
`RAISE_CHANGE_NOTICES` in `src/jelly/native.ts` to true and declare it in `jelly.notices` (jelly refuses an
undeclared notice). What jelly
has no contract for yet — Allow and Not now on jelly's own card, the hint's `actions` growing `allow` and `decline`,
and ending the task with jelly's conversation — is on issues #3 and #5.

## Settings

`jelly.contributes.settings` declares two of the plugin's options. Jelly draws each as a choice, never as free text,
and writes the value into the option of the same name:

- `access`, a choice of three: **Allowed** (`all`, the default), **Ask before changes** (`ask-changes`) and **Read
  only** (`read-only`), with Jelly's own line for each.
- `browser`, a choice of two: **Your browser** (`real`, the default), the person's own Chrome, gated per task as above,
  and **Separate browser** (`managed`), a Chromium with its own profile, which is not gated.

Both sets are the options parser's own, so Jelly never saves a value the plugin refuses. A Jelly that does not know
declared choices (before app#1301) refuses the whole declaration. `headless` and `verifyBinary` (switches), `path` and
`chromiumPath` (paths) and `scope` (an object) are not declared. `test/unit/jelly.test.ts` checks the settings against
Jelly's setting rules, restated in `test/support/jelly-settings.ts` (a shared copy, pinned by `scripts/check-copies.mjs`),
and each declared value against the options parser.

# Scripts

The plugin exposes `browse.tools`, one method per known browse tool, so a script can call them with no model. The
session is created for the script with an agent (`opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"…","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'`, with `data.id` kept), and the body is
`{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{…}}}`: both keys are required, and no other key is allowed. Give the project as the session's `location`: a session made without one belongs to the service's default location, where the project's agents may not exist, and each call then fails `Agent not found`.

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/browse.tools/session_list -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{}}}'
```

`describe` lists every method with its class and, given a session, the permission the call would get:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/browse.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>"}}'
```

A `browse` result comes back as `{ output?, text }`: the tool's structured content when it has any, and its text parts
joined by newlines.

## Methods

| Method | Class | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | read | allow |
| `session_list` | read | allow |
| `secrets_list` | read | allow |
| `secrets_status` | read | allow |
| `tabs_cleanup` | destructive | allow |

| `session_adopt` | write | allow |
| `session_reset` | destructive | allow |
| `session_delete` | destructive | allow |
| `settings` | write | allow |
| `execute` | destructive | allow |
| `secrets_run` | destructive | allow |
| `secrets_refresh` | destructive | allow |
| `session_allowlist` | destructive | allow |
| `network` | export | allow |
| `recording` | export | allow |
| `flight_recorder` | export | allow |

**Every tool is allowed by default**, and so is a tool browse adds later (`browse_*`). A script gets the same default:
the tools RPC resolves the rule before dispatch, and the default allow *is* that allow, so a script can call every
method without a prompt.

**The three captures run by default, and a script can start one with no model turn and no prompt.** That is a
deliberate default, and it is worth weighing before you grant a script a session:

- `network` captures authenticated request and response **headers and bodies** from the user's logged-in session
  (credential-bearing fields become references, the rest is in clear) and writes a redacted HAR to a path the script
  chooses.
- `recording` records the real tab's **pixels**, and its **audio** in tab-capture mode, to a path the script chooses.
- `flight_recorder` keeps a rolling buffer of the tab's pixels and `save_last` writes a clip to a path the script
  chooses.

The artifacts stay where the script writes them, for as long as the file exists. A path outside the project also needs
an `external_directory` allow, because OpenCode asks for that as well as for the capture's own action before anything
is written: `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "<the captures folder>/*", "effect": "allow" }`. A refusal
that names `external_directory` costs nothing, because nothing was written.

To restrict a script, do one of three:

1. set the plugin's `access` option to `"ask-changes"` (every changing method asks, and a script's ask is refused
   because no one can answer it) or `"read-only"` (every changing method is denied);
2. give the script's agent its own `deny` rule for a method, such as
   `{ "action": "browse_recording", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }`;
3. turn on scoped mode, which denies the session tools that could leave the pinned session.

Only `allow` runs. An `ask` is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and no prompt, because a script cannot answer one; a
`deny` is refused and the method is absent from the agent's tool list. A saved "Always allow" does not authorize a
script: a script's grant is a rule in config, or a Jobs run session.

## The location

Run the command in the project whose agent you mean, and send the call to that location explicitly:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/<id>/<method> -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{…}'
```

Without it the call goes to the service's default location and fails `rpc.unavailable` if the plugin is not loaded
there. The HTTP equivalents are the `location[directory]` query parameter and the same header. `describe` reports the
`location` that answered and a `locationHint`.

A location unloads after OpenCode's idle timeout. If a scheduled script gets `rpc.unavailable` from a location that was
loaded before, send the call again once: the request loads the location. Jobs keeps its own location loaded.

## Refusals

A refusal is the RPC error `failed` with `data: { code, next }`:

| Code | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | the rule resolves to ask, or a deny hides the method | add an allow rule for the method to the session's agent or to the session |
| `SESSION_UNKNOWN` | the session does not exist in this location | create the session in the location you mean, and pass its id |
| `SESSION_AGENT_REQUIRED` | the session names no agent | create a session that names an agent |
| `TOOL_UNAVAILABLE` | OpenCode does not list the method's tool now | call `describe` to see the methods there are |
| `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | browse returned an error | read the first line, and run `/browse-doctor` |
| `CANCELLED` | the call was cancelled | call the method again if you still need the result |
| `BINARY_MISSING`, `BINARY_UNVERIFIED` | the pinned binary is absent or does not match its digest | run `/browse-install`, then restart OpenCode |
| `SERVER_CONFLICT`, `SERVER_LEGACY` | another server holds the `browse` name, or an older one is configured | remove it, then run `opencode reload` |
| `SCOPE_UNREACHABLE`, `SCOPE_LOST` | the pinned session cannot be reached, or was lost | run `/browse-doctor` and follow its next step |

Every other code the plugin raises is in `docs/configuration.md`, with its one next step.

Known limit (`DC-2`, shared across the family): a saved "Always allow" answer from an earlier session is not part of the
agent and session rules, so it does not authorize an ad hoc script.

- At Allowed (`all`), the default, every tool runs without asking, declared or not, whatever its `effect`.
- At Ask before changes (`ask-changes`), a `readOnly` tool runs, and every other tool asks first, including a tool this plugin does not declare.

- A declared `effect` of `allow` changes nothing: the tool follows the access choice and its `readOnly`.

- A declared `effect` of `deny` turns the tool off at Ask before changes and at Read only, and changes nothing at Allowed.
- An action listed in `asks` asks first at Ask before changes and at Read only, and never at Allowed.
- A tool named with one `*`, such as another account's `plaud-*.get_file`, follows the same rules as a tool named in full.
- A choice the person makes for one tool wins over the access choice and the declared `effect`.
- jelly leaves out a key it does not know at the top level of the `jelly` block, and reads the rest.
- jelly refuses the plugin for a key it does not know inside anything it reads, such as a tool, a sign-in or a setting.
